objective: Harden ordinary teaching operation export routes so unsafe export manifest identifiers are rejected before external course-management readback.

codeReferences.summary: The export route now resolves and validates manifestId before external course-management readback or ownership checks.
The route-level export manifest safe-id guard returns a stable redacted 400 error for unsafe manifest ids.
Regression proves unsafe export manifest ids do not trigger external readback or ownership checks.

redGreenEvidence.observedFailure: The route returned 404 'Teaching export manifest not found.' after the unsafe manifest id entered the external readback path.

securityPosture.ordinaryTeachingRoute: Export manifest download now rejects unsafe manifest ids before external course-management snapshot readback, local manifest lookup, ownership lookup, or file response generation.
securityPosture.rbacBoundary: Teacher authentication and production auth-provider readiness still run first; unsafe export manifest ids are denied immediately after that trusted identity boundary and before resource lookup.
securityPosture.redaction: The unsafe path-like manifest id, storage token variable value, external origin, and local data directory are not echoed in the response.
securityPosture.productionPersistence: The regression uses production-style external teaching-operation and course-management storage configuration and proves no external readback request is made for unsafe manifest ids.

aggregateEnterpriseGateImpact.summary: This closes a narrow ordinary teaching direct-call readback gap in export manifest retrieval. The full enterprise gate still requires same-run owner-approved production evidence for env placement, deployment, storage, ordinary teaching route/browser smokes, app-auth readiness, browser workflow smoke, and live provider generation.
